- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below peak for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 0.5–1.5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model frequently underreacts to sentiment shifts; if sentiment flips from bullish to bearish, delay forecast adjustment by 1–2 days and reduce slope of decline.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overfit recent volatility; apply mean reversion bias: if 10-day moving average is >10% above recent 30-day mean, reduce forecast by 1–2%.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is flat, model often predicts minor drift; forecast should be anchored to 3–5 day average unless sentiment shifts.
